$comment: Floors on what each suite group must run, and ceilings on what it may skip.
Read by scripts/run-suites.mjs; surfaced per job by the ci gate in the workflow.
Why a count and not just an exit code: when journey.test.ts cannot reach a database
its beforeAll throws, and vitest reports '3 failed' files but '62 skipped' tests. A
suite that stopped running therefore looks one word away from a suite that ran, in
the line a person actually reads. The exit code separates them only because the hook
throws -- one try/catch in the wrong place and the numbers are all that is left.
minPassed is a ratchet: adding tests raises the actual above the floor and passes,
while a suite that quietly stops running drops below it and fails. Raising a floor
is optional. Lowering one has to be a deliberate line in a diff.
maxSkipped is set to exactly what is skipped today, so a new skip fails the build. A
skipped test is a test nobody runs, and the only two in this repository are skipped
because they need a credential CI cannot have.
Measured in CI, not on a laptop, and that distinction cost a red build. The machine
this was first measured on had OPENAI_API_KEY injected, so the retrieval test gated
behind it ran there and skipped in CI: 216 passed / 2 skipped locally against 215 / 3
in CI. A floor of 216 would have been a floor that only holds where a key happens to
exist. CI is the authority for these numbers; a local run may exceed them.
openAiGated: how many tests in the group are gated on OPENAI_API_KEY and therefore swap
sides depending on the machine. minPassed and maxSkipped are the KEYLESS figures, which
is what CI sees; a machine with a key must pass that many more and skip that many fewer.
Added because a key-gated test landed twice in one evening and the second one left main
red -- worse than a wrong number, because a permanently red trunk hides the next real
regression behind a benign one. If you add a key-gated test, raise openAiGated rather
than the ceiling: one number then holds on both machines.

unit.whySkipped: packages/export: the near-limit archive test behind PHOTOGRAPHIC_NEAR_LIMIT_DISK. It writes a multi-gigabyte archive to a temporary file and reads it back with a zip implementation that is not ours, which is minutes of disk rather than seconds of CPU -- too slow for every pull request and the only thing that proves our writer and a third-party reader agree about zip64. Run it when the zip64 code changes: PHOTOGRAPHIC_NEAR_LIMIT_DISK=1 pnpm --filter @photographic/export test

db.whySkipped: packages/db, keyless: two tls.test.ts tests behind LIVE_SUPABASE=1, and two behind OPENAI_API_KEY -- retrieval.test.ts and search-quality.test.ts, the second of which arrived with PR #16 and is what left main red. All four need a credential CI cannot have. The floor is CI's number, measured on the run for 0957dce: 212 passed / 4 skipped without a key, against 214 / 2 on a machine that has one.
